clue.text: Where to see the stars come out?

definitions.text: Where to see the stars come out?

parts.words: Where to see the stars come out?
parts.note: the stars are not in the night sky but actors leaving a theatre by the performers' exit at the back

explanation.surface: A stargazer asks where best to watch the night sky light up.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre stars leave by the backstage exit, where fans wait to see them emerge.

clue.text: Board on a universal stage setting

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging or a boardroom table
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A plank laid across a general-purpose stage forms part of the set.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a stage scene of motionless actors, a staged picture or setting.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's first to pay attention

indicators.note: the first of Gordon's letters is wanted, signalled by the word first after it

parts.note: to pay attention is to listen

explanation.surface: Flash Gordon, the comic-strip hero, is the first to heed a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash Gordon reads as the space hero's name, but Flash is the definition and Gordon only supplies G.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or flash with reflected light, a near synonym for shining briefly.

clue.text: Tum bared, made ready for a tattoo

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are prepared and rearranged, so a reshuffle is signalled

explanation.surface: Someone bares their belly ready to be inked at a tattoo parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattoo' suggests ink on a bared tummy; here it is the military drumming sense. 'made ready' rearranges TUM BARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo in the military sense is a drum signal or rhythmic beating, such as a drummed call to quarters.

clue.text: Harvester gets slipped disc in the back

indicators.note: the disc letters sit inside the word for the back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: a slipped disc is one moved out of place, so the letters for disc are turned round

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record, a disc

explanation.surface: A farm labourer suffers a slipped disc in the lower back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an injured farmhand; 'slipped' is the reversal signal applied to the disc, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper is someone or something that cuts and gathers a crop, a harvester.

clue.text: Chopin's sole piano composition?

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain piece was Chopin's only work for piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin wrote many polonaises, so the question mark admits the whole clue is playful; 'composition' rearranges SOLE PIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A polonaise is a stately Polish dance form, famously written for solo piano by Chopin.

clue.text: Vast, cold area of Southern European peninsula

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Describes a huge chilly region in southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the cold area in Spain; in fact S plus IBERIA builds the Russian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the immense, freezing region of northern Asia within Russia.

clue.text: China's art-form is revolutionary

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of the preceding words are reshaped

explanation.surface: Claims that Chinese art is radical and new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art-form' reads as one word, but 'form' alone is the anagram signal for CHINAS ART; 'revolutionary' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist, seeking to overthrow all government, is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Feeling of joy in Sibelius's fourth movement

indicators.note: only the fourth letter of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: motion is movement

explanation.surface: A listener feels joy in the fourth movement of a Sibelius symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests a symphony section; it simply means MOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy is an example of an emotion, a strong feeling.

clue.text: Inclined to be evasive

definitions.meaning: indirect and not straightforward in speech

explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means both slanting and roundabout or indirect in what is said.

clue.text: Individual inside jetty is a developer

indicators.note: the word for an individual goes within the word for jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A property developer is singled out standing on a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer develops new ground or ideas, one who first opens something up.

clue.text: Slipping pieces in a personal column?

definitions.text: Slipping pieces in a personal column?

parts.words: Slipping pieces in a personal column?
parts.note: the personal column is not a newspaper's small ads but one's own spine, whose pieces can slip

explanation.surface: Someone slips small notices into a newspaper's personal ads.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones of the spinal column, which can slip, as in a slipped disc between them.

clue.text: Story to support a fellow showing friendliness

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

parts.note: a fable is a story

explanation.surface: A tale backing up a companion shows warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to, the manner of a warm person.

clue.text: A King and I production, in new setting, is fantastic

indicators.note: the letters from A King and I go inside the word for new

parts.note: fresh means new
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A new staging of the musical The King and I is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' and 'setting' dress the musical The King and I; A, K and I stay in order inside FRESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Freakish means strange and unreal, in the sense of fantastic or bizarre.

clue.text: Spanish gooseberry expected, girl turned back

parts.note: due means expected

indicators.note: the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish chaperone was expected, but the girl turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: A gooseberry, in British slang, is an unwanted third person with a couple; here it is a chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman chaperoning girls in a Spanish family, a chaperone or 'gooseberry'.

clue.text: Last month, public speaker; now, a wallpaperer

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the last month
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Someone who spoke publicly last month now hangs wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator paints and papers rooms, so hanging wallpaper is the job.

clue.text: He found himself winning on the pools

definitions.text: He found himself winning on the pools

parts.words: He found himself winning on the pools
parts.note: not a football-pools jackpot: the mythical youth found his own reflection in a pool so attractive that he fell for it

explanation.surface: A man struck lucky with the football pools, a British betting game.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British weekly betting coupon; 'winning' here means charming.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth fell in love with his own handsome reflection in a pool.

clue.text: Collection of charts in which sea-salt may be worked

indicators.note: working something reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sea salt being worked in a salt pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are books of maps, so a set of them is a collection of charts.

clue.text: England's openers failed badly in these shots

parts.note: the opening two letters of England

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen fail with poor strokes at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' and 'shots' suggest cricket batsmen; the shots are gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfilade is gunfire sweeping along a line of troops from end to end.

clue.text: One in tugs with villainous actors

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the word for tugs

parts.note: to heave is to pull or tug
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone on a tugboat sails with a gang of villains.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavies are actors cast as villains, the bad guys of stage and screen.

clue.text: Backstitch in open-work fabric is the most modern

indicators.note: the reversed stitch goes inside the fabric word

parts.note: net is an open-mesh fabric
read as back plus stitch: the word sew, meaning stitch, turned backwards

explanation.surface: A backstitch in lace is the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Backstitch is a real embroidery stitch, but here it splits into 'back' and 'stitch', a reversed sewing word set inside NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest thing is the most recent, the most up to date.

clue.text: Spring collection properly put together

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: A spring fashion collection is neatly assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-set means firmly and properly joined or built.

clue.text: Hearing one could have jam on it

definitions.meaning: a sitting of a court or committee

definitions.text: one could have jam on it

explanation.definitionFit: A session is both a formal sitting and a period of playing music, as in a jam session.

clue.text: Bid too high in accomplished style

parts.note: over means finished or accomplished
to style someone is to call them by a title

explanation.surface: An overreaching bid made with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, to overcall is to bid over an opponent; the clue takes it as bidding too high.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcall in bridge is a bid above an opponent's bid, hence bidding higher.

clue.text: King in majestic uprising is even more grand

indicators.note: the king's letter goes within the reversed word
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: regal means majestic
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king in a majestic revolt grows grander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns REGAL into LAGER; R goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger means bigger, a comparative of great size like grander.

clue.text: Highly skilful daring young man

parts.note: recalls the daring young man on the flying trapeze, whose skill is shown high in the air

explanation.surface: Praises a very able and bold young fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'The Daring Young Man on the Flying Trapeze' supplies the picture; 'Highly' means up high.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerialist is a trapeze artist or tightrope walker performing high up.

clue.text: Counsellor, these days, takes a face-protector

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: A modern counsellor wears a face shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser gives counsel, so a counsellor is one.

clue.text: Standard bargain, this vegetable

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
a snip is a bargain in British slang

explanation.surface: A good deal on this standard vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Excessive employment of old poetry around university

indicators.note: the poetry word goes round the university letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Too much use is made of old poetry at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse is using something too much, excessive employment of it.

clue.text: Taking exception to putting on show without a beginner

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word for putting on show

parts.note: presenting means putting on show

explanation.surface: Objecting to staging a show without a novice in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginner' suggests a learner; here it is the word's first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to take offence or exception at it.
